page: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the ESv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear trade-off between compute power and memory capacity. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1171.0 and average single-threaded compression speeds, such as 23.95 GB/sec in gzip. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks are constrained by the dual-vCPU allocation. The multi-core Geekbench score is 1440.0, and the Passmark CPU score is 2207.61, both falling into lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 11.55 GB/sec for large-block reads and 8.77 GB/sec for large-block writes. Database operations and web serving throughput are also limited, with Redis SET operations reaching 1.67 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 1.98 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-2s_v4 is structured for workloads that require a large memory footprint but have minimal CPU demands. This resource density allows users to avoid paying for unneeded compute cores while securing 64.0 GB of RAM. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads. Appropriate use cases include caching layers, small memory-bound databases, lightweight enterprise applications, and simple data buffering tasks where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck.
